approvedDesign.title: Arrival at the entry: 35% of each hostile and patrol group arrives 45 s after first contact and moves toward the squad; a retreat order or break-off cancels it
approvedDesign.problem: The board offers Reinforcements ("A second garrison arrives partway through, from the wrong direction") at x1.3 and nothing arrives: the id appears only in its table row (missiontypes.js:823). A player cannot read when "partway" is, where "the wrong direction" is, how many come, or what to do about it. The clock has to be an event the player can already see. First contact (a fight has opened or a hostile has a line to a squad member, Field.contacted, field.js:1477) happens in 100% of the harness contracts at a median of 75 in-game s (15 real s; p10 30, p90 151), and it is the event that ends the free "Call it off" window, so a countdown that starts there can be read on the paper, in the side panel and on the map. A fraction of mission.duration is not such a clock: the duration is an estimate (median 840 in-game s at levels 1-4 on these types) and the median contract ends at 312 s (p10 144, p90 822), so a release at half of it (420 s) would come after the end of more than half of the contracts.
evidence: missiontypes.js:823-824 TWISTS.reinforcements (weight 12, reward 1.3, not duel); grep -w finds the id only in this row. Consumers that exist for other twists: field.js:2082 (night), sortie.js:503 (dry), field.js:1560 (hardcore).

field.js:1477 contacted(s) = counters.fights > 0 or any actor spotted (landed with loop-retreat; field.js:1222 counts fights, field.js:878 sets e.spotted). One definition of contact; this design reads it and adds a timestamp.

field.js:1727 arrivals() is the clock-driven spawner for deferred cast groups; field.js:1673 spawnGroup(s, g, n); mapgen.js:340 marks a group deferred when it has per or a temporal at; mapgen.js:33 has the entry slot, so at: entry is placed by around(sl, zones.entry, n, 6).

field.js:798 chooseGoals: nest, garrison, wandering, ambush, patrol and quarry hostiles stand still unless they see, remember or are roused; only the default branch (waves, endless) calls hunt() unconditionally. A group added to a nest contract would not move toward the squad unless it takes that branch.

field.js:1375 (window shut, 30%) and field.js:1582 (escalate, 50%) respawn a share of EVERY hostile and patrol group in map.spawns with no check for deferred groups, so an added cast group is cloned unless it is skipped.

field.js:1784 descend() rebuilds map.spawns with MG.build. Maps with floors > 1 are warren (2), dungeon (4) and stronghold (2) (missiontypes.js:74-76), and retrieval, rescue, raid, recon, assassination, capture, extermination and expedition roll on them. A fired flag kept on the spawn would be lost on the stairs and the group would fire again on the next floor; spawns are rebuilt in cast order, so the flag is carried by cast index (3 lines).

field.js:1267 kill() counts kills by role; field.js:1521 rawWin reads killed(s, a.of); missiontypes.js:352 extermination asks 80% of total(cast, hostile); :768 the silence atom counts patrol kills; :1047 describe().hostiles; :234 total(). All of them mean "the written bodies", so total() ignores groups with arrive and arrival kills are counted under their own key.

quests.js:116 rolls trial contracts with mt.roll(type, { level, name }); roll() has no trial option and rollTwists no filter, so star trials (the solo road included) draw every row. The pursuit lens assumes quests.js already passes trial: true; it does not.

sortie.js:259 (launch) takes the pseudoZone species from s.actors, and deferred groups have no actors at launch, so Missions.prepare would plan loadouts without the arrival groups (pseudoZone's id includes species.length, so the cache key changes when they are added).

bestiary.js:201-212 brief() builds one row per species / level / per / handle from mission.cast; sortie.js:889 missionCard and :1045 briefBox print the rows. A cast group with an arrive field reaches the card and the brief with no new screen; nameCast (sortie.js:61) gives each cloned group its own species of the same tier and theme.
field.js:382 withdraw(s, why, ordered) sets s.withdrew; both the squad's own break-off (broken()) and the retreat order (field.js:1487 retreat) go through it, so one test (s.withdrew) covers both.

Seeded roll check (scratchpad arr3/rollcheck.js, 600 rolls, two trees): moving rollTwists above the cast changes no draw order (spec.cast and spec.terms draw no random numbers, missiontypes.js:330-800): 499 rolls identical, 89 differ only where Reinforcements or Infested was rolled, 12 differ only on duel / dungeon / escort, whose legal twist pool changed.

Node check of the mechanism in the prototype (arr3/fieldtest.js, 16 assertions, all pass): the group is deferred at start; it fires at contactAt + 45 exactly once; save / restore at +20 keeps contactAt and fired; a retreat order 10 s after contact cancels it; escalate spawns no arrival group but still respawns written groups; total() and the extermination target (12 of 15 written bodies) ignore arrival groups; arrival counts equal max(1, round(count x 0.35)).

Measured on test/sortie.harness.js (the game's own scripts booted by test/game.boot.js, real combat.js, board -> launch -> skip -> settle; gearless 3-5 star random-class squads of 4; levels 1-4; both arms on the same seed per contract; 1320 paired contracts on the 11 legal types): without the twist 60.7% won and 0.41 deaths per contract; with the arrival and the hold rule 54.2% and 0.60; without the hold rule 0.23 extra deaths instead of 0.18. The arrival fired in 83% of contracts (97% without the hold rule) and reached the squad in 80% (93%). 14.3% of releases without the hold rule came after the squad had withdrawn; 24.2% came after it had started the walk home (phase leaving), 11.6% with the rule.
approvedDesign.change:
MODS (the table row, data only): reinforcements: { label: 'Reinforcements', weight: 12, reward: 1.25, not: ['duel', 'dungeon', 'escort', 'hold', 'siege'], trial: false, mods: { arrivals: [{ on: 'contact', delay: 45, from: 'entry', share: 0.35 }] } }. MT.modsOf defaults arrivals to [] and folds by concatenation, so another twist can add an entry with a different trigger. The desc is generated by MOD_TEXT.arrivals(entries, mission): "45 s (0:09) after the first sighting or fight, 35% of each hostile and patrol group (at least 1 body per group; about 5 bodies on this paper) arrives at the entry and moves toward the squad. Terms and bonuses count the written bodies only. A retreat order or a break-off cancels it." The body count follows the contract's intel through Bestiary.countText (at intel 0 the text gives the share and the delay only).

CONSUMERS.
(1) missiontypes.js. total() ignores groups with arrive. New pure arrivalCast(cast, arrivals): for each entry and each hostile or patrol group g of the written cast (not forSide, not already arrive) it emits { ...g, count: max(1, round(g.count * share)), at: from, arrive: { on, delay }, forTwist: id } without per, pack, from or species (for a per group g.count is one repetition). roll() moves 'const tw' above the cast at the same RNG position (verified above) and pushes arrivalCast(cast, mods.arrivals) after spec.terms, so win, lose and bonus atoms are those of the written contract. A twist whose effect came out empty is dropped from tw, so a contract never carries the tag and the multiplier without groups. MT.current(m) (u-honesty) also requires, for each twist with an arrivals mod, a cast group with forTwist === id, which stales board and held trial offers rolled before this lands. rollTwists(typeId, level, max, { trial }) skips rows with trial: false when trial is set; roll() takes trial; quests.js:116 passes trial: true.
(2) mapgen.js:340 deferred: !!(group.per || group.arrive || TEMPORAL.has(group.at)).
(3) field.js. start(), save() and restore() carry contactAt (null until set). arrivals() sets s.contactAt = s.clock on the first step at which contacted(s) is true. Then, for each s.map.spawns entry g with g.arrive and no g.fired, and only while s.withdrew is unset: due when s.clock >= s.contactAt + g.arrive.delay. On due: g.fired = s.clock (the spawn list is saved with the map, so a reload cannot fire twice), spawnGroup(s, g), and one log line with the body count and the distance in tiles from the group's first point to the nearest squad member. descend() copies g.fired across by cast index. spawnGroup / makeActor set march = true on bodies of a group with arrive; ACTOR_KEYS gets 'march'; chooseGoals (:798) becomes switch (e.march ? 'march' : m.pressure), so a marching body takes the default branch, hunt(), in every contract type. kill() (:1267) counts a march body under counters.killed.arrival instead of its role. The two respawn loops (:1375, :1582) skip groups with arrive.
(4) bestiary.js brief(): the arrive field goes into the row key and onto the row. sortie.js briefBox prints "arrives 0:09 after first contact, at the entry"; missionCard appends "+5 later" to the expect line from describe(), whose hostiles figure stops counting arrival groups (total()).
(5) sortie.js launch (:259): species gets one entry per body of each cast group with arrive, so Missions.prepare plans against them.
(6) sortie.js renderSide: one line under the portal line: "arrival after first contact", "arrival in 0:07", "arrival: 4 bodies, 34 tiles from the squad" or "arrival cancelled". fieldview.js drawMap: the label of the entry zone reads "arrival 0:07" while a group is pending (drawActors already draws unrevealed hostiles at alpha .38, so the group is visible once it exists).
(7) sortie.js settle() (:574): gs.field.twists[id] = { sent, won, dead }, the same shape as loop-ledger's gs.field.types and incremented in the same loop; the tag title prints it once sent > 0.
(8) test/sortie.harness.js: TWISTS=none|id[,id] pins the contract's twists (2 lines in contractOf) so one OUT file per arm pairs by type, level and seed. New test/twistprice.js prints the inputs of the price rule and exits 1 when the table value differs from the measured multiplier by more than 0.10 (a prototype of it ran on the files of this round). test/contracts.js: counts equal max(1, round(count x 0.35)); total() and terms identical with and without the twist; fire exactly once at contactAt + 45 across save / restore at +20; no fire after withdraw(); escalate and window-shut spawn no arrival group; descend does not fire a group twice; counters.killed.arrival; MT.current false for a mission with the id and no group.

CARD AND MAP. Card: tag "Reinforcements x1.25"; its title lists the factors ("25 + 30 x level 3 = 115 / Assassination x2.5 / Reinforcements x1.25") and the generated desc; the expect line lists the extra rows with "+N later". Brief: the arrival groups are their own rows, one per species, with the arrival text, subject to the contract's intel like every row. Map: the countdown on the entry zone, then ghost tokens at the entry that move toward the squad; the log gives the body count and the distance. Side panel: the arrival line above.

REWARD x1.25. The multiplier is a table value, set with one rule and checked by test/twistprice.js. Rule: a squad that takes the twist should end each attempt with the gems it would have had without it: pay0 + loot0 - 100 x dead0 = m x pay1 + loot1 - 100 x dead1, with pay and loot the harness's per-attempt means (a lost contract pays 0) and 100 the price of a summon (PULL_COST, game.js:8, printed on the Summon button). Inputs (11 legal types, 1320 paired contracts): wins 60.7 -> 54.2%, deaths 0.41 -> 0.60 per contract, fee per attempt 114.3 -> 98.4, loot per attempt 57.9 -> 68.6 gems: m = 1.24, rounded to 1.25. The same inputs with the death price at 50 / 150 / 200 gems give 1.15 / 1.33 / 1.43; ignoring loot, 1.35; with no death price, 1.05. Wound downtime is not in the price (loop-wounds is not built; the harness reports no wounds yet). The player's check: the card title itemises the factor, the brief lists the exact extra bodies, and the tag tooltip shows their own record with this complication (sent, won, people lost).

FREQUENCY. weight 12 (unchanged), not duel, dungeon, escort, hold, siege. Per contract under u-honesty's draw rule with all nine rows live (exact enumeration over a board of uniformly drawn types, arr3/freq.js): 2.3% at level 1, 3.5% at 5, 5.1% at 10, 6.8% at 15, 8.5% at 20, against 3.2 / 4.8 / 6.9 / 9.2 / 11.6% for the original row. The other twists move by 0.1 points or less. P(at least one on a board of 5): 11% at level 1, 16% at 5, 23% at 10, 30% at 15, 36% at 20.
approvedDesign.playerEffect: Before launch the paper states that each hostile and patrol group has 35% more bodies, that they come second and from the way in, and when; a player compares the squad against both fights on the same ground and against x1.25. During the run the player has one lever and it prevents deaths: the retreat order, with a countdown on the screen. Measured with the order given at the first calm moment (no open fight) at or after contact + k, on 330 paired contracts: deaths per contract without the arrival / with it are 0.41 / 0.58 with no order, 0.05 / 0.05 with the order at contact (k = 0), and 0.30 / 0.44 with the order 60 in-game s (12 real s) after contact. The order saves 0.36 deaths per contract at k = 0 without the arrival and 0.53 with it, and 0.11 / 0.14 at k = 60. It costs the contract: wins are 60% / 53% with no order, 1% / 2% at k = 0 and 20% / 19% at k = 60. The squad's own break-off cancels the arrival in the same way (191 of 1320 contracts never fired because the squad withdrew before +45 s; 28 because the contract ended first). Without any retreat the twist costs 0.18 deaths per contract and 6.4 win points.
approvedDesign.secondOrder: Retreat order (loop-retreat): contact starts two clocks, the end of the free call-off window and the release; a withdrawal cancels the release, so the order is worth more than before and the arrival never chases a squad that has already decided to leave (without that rule 14.3% of releases came after the withdrawal and the extra deaths were 0.23 instead of 0.18). Wounds (loop-wounds, WOUND_FROM 0.4): survivors whose lowest HP fell under 40% go from 18.0% to 21.7%, and contracts with such a survivor from 46.3% to 48.9%, so the twist feeds the downtime wave 2 introduces. Debrief: fights per contract 6.54 -> 7.89 (+21%), so casts spent per sortie rise with them; the stamina charge (25 + 1.5 x level in u-debrief) does not depend on fights. Permadeath: contracts with a death 21.0% -> 26.4%. Loadouts: the arrival groups' species are in the pseudoZone, so a brilliant mind plans resistances for them. Bestiary: arrival species enter Bestiary.record and noteSighting. Loot: kill drops rise (57.9 -> 68.6 gems per attempt) and are in the price. Hardcore: the escalation and window-shut respawns skip arrival groups, so the two do not stack their spawns. Night: halves sight, so contact comes later and so does the release. Side jobs: Leave no witnesses counts written patrol kills only (total()). Tactics: the retreat play ("a step back") falls back to the way in, which is where the group appears; it fires rarely, so no effect was measurable. Pairs: measured on 330 paired contracts (11 legal types, 30 each). No resupply alone: wins 60 -> 57%, deaths 0.41 -> 0.56, m = 1.02 (n = 330); with the arrival added on top: wins 57 -> 50%, deaths 0.56 -> 0.81, m = 1.34 (n = 330). Night alone: wins 60 -> 61%, deaths 0.41 -> 0.44, m = 0.90 (n = 330); with the arrival added: wins 61 -> 56%, deaths 0.44 -> 0.60, m = 1.16 (n = 330). Against the plain base, No resupply plus the arrival: wins 60 -> 50%, deaths 0.41 -> 0.81, m = 1.36 (n = 330). The board multiplies table values (No resupply 1.25 x 1.25 = 1.56), so the pair is paid more than its measured neutral value; deaths add a little more than the sum of the two parts. Side finding for the pricing rule: by the same rule No resupply alone measures 1.02 and Night 0.90, against table values of 1.25 and 1.15, so the live rows are not priced by it either.
approvedDesign.risks: Build after u-honesty (modsOf, MOD_TEXT entries as functions of (value, mission), MT.current) and loop-retreat (contacted, retreat); approve at most one of reinforcements-a and reinforcements-b, which are alternatives on one table row. Harness caveats: plain characters without gear or potions, so absolute deaths are upper bounds (base 0.41 deaths per contract); confirm on a real save as loop-wounds step 7 does. The multiplier is an average over a wide spread: per type, the same rule on the held design gives assassination 2.58, capture 0.95, expedition 0.89, extermination 1.37, pursuit 1.00, raid 1.22, recon 1.14, rescue 1.60, retrieval 0.90, sabotage 1.39, survival 1.28; assassination alone is where base deaths are already 1.7 per contract (n = 120 per type, so single types are noisy). The release is inert where contact comes late or the squad is gone first (fires / reaches: assassination fires 78% reaches 72%; pursuit fires 74% reaches 74%; raid fires 69% reaches 68%; recon fires 79% reaches 76%; survival fires 76% reaches 70%). hold and siege are excluded on a stated criterion: the arrival reached the squad in fewer than half of the runs (hold 42%, siege 31%) and deaths did not move; the criterion is a harness reading and drifts with combat changes. dungeon is excluded on a reading of the code, not a measurement: descend() drops every actor that is not ours, so a group released on one floor is left behind on the stairs. escort is excluded on the harness: median first contact 200 in-game s against a median end of 220 s, and 75% of its contracts (n = 20, levels 1-4) are over before contact + 45. On the earlier private runner the nearest squad member was under 20 in-game s of walking from the entry in 9.8% of releases (survival 74%, raid 21%, every other type 7% or less); that was not repeated on the harness. If a squad holding ground next to the way in is unwanted, hold the release until no squad member is within sight + 2 tiles of the entry, for at most 30 s (not measured). Extermination: written bodies only count toward the 80%, so killing arrivals does not shorten the job. Dials: delay 20 s: deaths 0.41 -> 0.69, wins 60 -> 53%, fires 96%, reaches 92%, m 1.32 (n = 330); delay 45 s: deaths 0.41 -> 0.63, wins 60 -> 51%, fires 84%, reaches 82%, m 1.36 (n = 330); delay 90 s: deaths 0.41 -> 0.53, wins 60 -> 55%, fires 69%, reaches 66%, m 1.17 (n = 330) (11 types, 30 contracts per type, paired with the same base). The death price (50 to 200 gems) moves the multiplier from about 1.15 to 1.4, so the table value is good to about +/-0.10 whatever the sampling error (+/-0.05).
approvedDesign.response:
Design attack. (1) "Mostly a bigger fight": accepted in part. The arrival now has a counter that prevents deaths: a retreat order or break-off cancels it, the countdown is on screen, and the sweep above gives the order's value with and without the twist. (2) "+0.16 deaths priced at 200 gems, which the user does not accept as a price": replaced. The price uses PULL_COST (game.js:8, 100 gems), counts loot, and is stated as a table value with the per-twist record as the check, not as a derivation the player must follow; the rule is one function in test/twistprice.js and prints its alternatives beside it. (3) "14% of firings after the squad withdrew": confirmed on the harness (14.3% of releases) and removed by holding the release while s.withdrew is set; the measured effect is in the numbers above. (4) Trials: verified that quests.js:116 passes no trial flag and roll() has no such option, so the plumbing is added here with the field name the pursuit lens uses (trial: false). (5) Arrival kills counted toward extermination: fixed by total() and counters.killed.arrival, so killing arrivals no longer shortens the job. Demands: trial: false (done); hold on withdrew (done, measured); written bodies only (done); x1.25 as a data value with the record as check (done); one ACTOR_KEYS flag, 'march', consumed by one chooseGoals line, and any follower design (hunted) can set the same flag.
Engineering attack. Stale offers: MT.current extended, and an empty twist is dropped at roll time. describe().hostiles: total() ignores arrival groups and the card prints "+N later". Kill quota: counters.killed.arrival. RNG order: not changed (seeded comparison above). Inert types: hold and siege excluded on the reach criterion; the rest priced as an average with the spread stated. Pricing rule: one rule for the lens, reproducible with test/twistprice.js. Private runner: replaced by test/sortie.harness.js with paired seeds. Defects found while checking and fixed in the design: descend() rebuilds spawns and would have fired the group again on the next floor of any warren, dungeon or stronghold map (fired is carried by cast index); the two respawn loops clone every hostile group (skipped).

verdicts.attack: It is mostly a bigger fight: 35% more bodies, printed on the paper, with a timer and a direction. The decision it adds is the timing of the retreat order, which u-retreat already provides; the column only raises that lever's value. +0.16 deaths per run (+63%) and 20.7% of runs with a death for x1.25 prices a death at 200 gems, which the user does not accept as a price. 14% of firings land after the squad has already withdrawn, so a squad that broke off from a lost fight walks into the column at the entry: the worst permadeath case is the one the design does not treat. Trials are not excluded, and a one-body solo trial gets at least one extra body per written group. Column kills count toward the extermination quota.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: arrivals() field.js:1702 and cued(at) :1705, spawnGroup :1648, mapgen deferral :340 and TEMPORAL :45, ZONE_SLOT entry :33 and zoneNames adding g.at :232-233, so at: 'entry' is placed by around(sl, zones.entry, n, 6) :334; chooseGoals pressure switch :797-810 where only the default branch hunts unconditionally; the window-shut and escalate re-spawn loops :1373 and :1557 set no goal; descend keeps only ours :1771; look() sets spotted and raises :874-881; openSkirmish :1219; brief rows bestiary.js:201-212; launch species from s.actors sortie.js:257 with deferred groups absent at start (field.js:2063); rollLoot gems do not read the body's level (missions.js:242). Scratchpad arrivals/results/final-n100 re-aggregated: base 69.5%/0.258 (n=1500), reinf_a over 15 types 64.9%/0.423; the 13-type figures 68.6%/0.251 to 64.8%/0.410 are consistent with that. Frequency figures use today's rule, not u-honesty's; the difference is under 0.5 points.
verdicts.demand: Add trial: false so no star trial carries it. Hold the release while s.withdrew is set (a squad that has already broken off is not punished a second time) or measure and state deaths in that case separately. Count only written bodies toward kill quotas, or say on the card that column kills count. State the x1.25 as a data value on the row with the per-twist record as the player's check; do not present R = 200 as a derivation the player can follow. Name the arriving actors' field flag the same as the pursuit lens's (one key in ACTOR_KEYS for 'moves on its own trigger').

verdicts.attack: Three things the proposal does not handle. (1) Stale offers: the column is added to mission.cast at roll time, so every board offer (re-rolled every 6 minutes, sortie.js:97) and every held trial offer (quests.js:112 keeps the pair until the star changes) rolled before this lands carries the tag and no column; only hunted-a proposes an MT.current cast check. (2) describe().hostiles (missiontypes.js:1047) sums hostile+patrol+mark counts in m.cast, so the card's hostile figure includes the column while the brief lists it as 'later'. (3) The win quota for extermination (kill 80% of the written count, :352) is met by column kills because counters.killed counts by role; the builder admits it and prices it in rather than fixing it. roll() has to compute tw before the cast (today tw is read at :954, after terms at :952), which changes RNG order for every seeded harness. On hold, siege and survival the column fires in 74-88% and reaches in 52-72%, so 1.25 is paid on contracts where it does nothing. The price rule (R = 200 plus drop income) is one of three different rules across the lenses. Measured on a private runner with gearless parties, not on test/sortie.harness.js.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: row at :823; arrivals() :1702 with per/cued at :1705; spawnGroup :1648; mapgen deferred :340 and ZONE_SLOT entry :33, around :271; zoneNames :226-238 adds cast at names, so an 'entry' zone is created and the column is placed around it; the window-shut respawn :1373-1376 and escalate :1557-1560 iterate every hostile/patrol spawn group; chooseGoals switch at :797 with hunt() in the default branch; look() :874-881; brief :201-212; launch species :257; descend drops hostiles :1770; save() stores map.spawns :1993. Scratchpad proj2 diff matches (arrive groups, march flag, contactAt in look and openSkirmish, SWARMED positive branch, mapgen dark slot and deferred). results/final-n100 aggregated by me: base n 1500 69.5% / 0.258 (exact match), reinf_a 64.9% / 0.423 over 15 types, consistent with the quoted 13-type 64.8% / 0.410. dry1.txt matches the Night/No resupply figures exactly. Frequencies: my simulation of the current rule gives reinforcements 3.1/4.8/7.1/11.9% at L1/5/10/20 against the quoted 3.4/4.8/7.2/12.2.
verdicts.demand: After u-honesty and u-retreat. Add the stale-offer check (MT.current compares the twist's expected cast groups), exclude march bodies from describe().hostiles and from the written kill quota (or print that they count), and skip arrive groups in both respawn loops as written. Build the arrive/march plumbing as the one cue-spawn mechanism the hunted and trap designs also use (see conflicts). Reproduce the 1300-run comparison on test/sortie.harness.js and price with the agreed rule before 1.25 is fixed.

sharedRules: Shared rules the user approved for every complication: (1) one price rule: the multiplier keeps expected gems per attempt equal, counting a death at PULL_COST (100 gems), R = p0/p1 + (d1 - d0) x 100 / (p1 x W0), rounded up to the next 0.05; (2) every number is re-measured on test/sortie.harness.js (add TWISTS=, GEAR=1 options if missing), not on a private runner; (3) at most one body-adding complication per contract (reinforcements, hunted, trap, turncoat, infested) until pairs are measured; (4) log lines state what spawned, where, at what distance and which term changed, in the engineering register; (5) trial: false on every row that adds bodies, threaded through quests.js.

conflicts: Three pricing conventions for the same quantity. Terrain prices a death at PULL_COST 100 gems and rounds up to 0.05; arrivals prices it at 200 gems plus kill drops; pursuit uses the relative rise in deaths with no formula. Same-sized effects get different multipliers: hunted-a +0.11 deaths per run -> x1.4, reinforcements-a +0.16 -> x1.25, infested-a +0.14 -> x1.50, trap-a +0.012 -> x1.15, storm-a +0.03 -> x1.05. None of the multipliers is derivable by the player from anything on screen (numbers-must-be-traceable); the per-twist record all three propose as the check is specified three ways (gs.field.twists { sent, won, dead } in terrain and arrivals; 'u-ledger can add' in pursuit) and u-ledger part A defines only gs.field.types. One owner, one R stated as data, one record shape.

Exit-route stacking. reinforcements-a (column from the entry 45 s after contact), hunted-a and hunted-b (a body trailing the squad), trap-a (a mark at the way home) and turncoat-a (the ward at the far end) all add bodies to the walk out, where the pursuit lens measured most deaths already occur. rollTwists allows two twists per contract (missiontypes.js:863, max 2) and no proposal measured any pair; the multipliers multiply (1.25 x 1.4 = 1.75) while the deaths very likely compound. Hardcore pairs are treated four different ways (trap-a skips once escalated, reinforcements-a skips arrival groups in the escalation re-spawn, infested-b doubles the escalation re-spawn through the swollen count, storms scale the escape window) and none is measured.

hunted-b and reinforcements-a are the same mechanism (a hostile group released behind the squad that reaches it on the way out); the pursuit builder says approve one. hunted-a's dominant effect (the squad bumps into a trailing elite) is the same mechanism again with one body.

Every proposal depends on u-honesty (MT.modsOf, MOD_TEXT, MT.current, TWIST_FULL, MT.factors, MT.payout), none of which exists in the code (grep finds no modsOf, MOD_TEXT, TWIST_FULL or MT.current in *.js). The mods fold table would carry about 15 keys with three fold semantics (multiply: move, damage, regen, sight; union/concat: noReach, status, arrivals; largest: promote; sum: swell; first: ambush, pit; plus follower/pack/turn/informant) and the pursuit rows add a cast: (lv) => [...] function on the TWISTS row that must never reach a saved mission. 'A twist is a table row plus one consumer' becomes a dispatch table; the fold rules need one owner and one test.

Field flags for 'a hostile that moves on its own trigger' are named four ways: march (reinforcements-a), stance 'trail' / 'pack' plus follows (hunted-a/b), spotted preset true (hunted), spottedAt (reinforcements-b); each adds ACTOR_KEYS entries and a chooseGoals branch. trapTick/ringTile are claimed by trap-a and trap-b and offered to Reinforcements. u-retreat's contacted() is edited by trap-a (adds s.trapped) and paralleled by reinforcements-a's contactAt; one definition of contact must serve the button, the column clock and the trap.

Frequency figures use different rules: terrain and pursuit quote u-honesty's odds x weight / 66; arrivals quotes today's rule with nine rows. With all rows live the legal pool exceeds 66 on every type (73 to 102 by weights proposed), so the honesty promise 'others unchanged until the weights sum to 66' fails slightly: by my exact two-draw calculation over the 16 types, at level 10 dry falls 6.5% to 5.9-6.1% and hardcore 5.5% to 5.0-5.2%. reinforcements-b (weight 24) and turncoat-a (weight 12) are weight hikes with no stated reason beyond compensating 'only'.

storm-a and storm-b are alternatives, but storm-b's bow rule changes every water-spell Wet outside storms (elements.js:170 is shared with spellcraft.js:54), while storm-a's lives only in combat.js; approving storm-b as written is a global balance change, approving storm-a is a twist-local special case. Both carry the same unpriced walking tax on window contracts.

Three private combat-backed runners (proto/exp/real.js, arrivals/run.js, pursuit/run.js) with three baselines (82.4%/0.10-0.115, 69.5%/0.258, 68.4%/0.251 deaths per run) that cannot be compared, while test/sortie.harness.js, the project's combat-backed harness (named in memory and in test/field.harness.js's header), was used by none; the terrain lens asks for 'a combat-backed runner in test/' that already exists.
missed: Trials. quests.js:116 rolls trial twists through MT.roll with no flag and no filter, so star trials, including the one-body solo road, draw every row. Only the pursuit lens adds trial: false, and it describes quests.js:116 as already passing trial: true, which it does not. Storm, Reinforcements (at least one extra body per written group against a single character), Infested and A trap on a solo trial are unmeasured and unexcluded.

The one-sided-fight quirk. sortie.js:158-160 gives noFightUntil = clock + 120 to every actor in a skirmish whose party or foes list is empty, so any hostile that catches a lone ward (no species, no fighter) is pacified for 120 in-game seconds. trap-a and turncoat-a both put a mark next to a ward, and nobody checked this path; it is also the reason 0 of 960 wards died, which the pursuit lens reports as a fact without the cause.

Phase 'leaving' is set both by withdraw() (field.js:383, a broken squad running) and by leave() (field.js:1875, the job done). The pursuit lens's premise that the walk out is 'the unthreatened part of a run' (76 of 100 deaths after leaving) counts post-withdrawal deaths; u-retreat's exitState reads s.withdrew and s.phase too. Any design that keys on 'the walk home' needs the two split.

The walking-speed term on window contracts. makePortal's shutsAt is mission.duration (field.js:1308); both storms scale only Hardcore's escape window, so escort and rescue (deadline true -> window) take the whole x0.8 tax: storm-b's own result file shows escort deaths 0.07 to 0.20-0.23 per run, unreported, and storm-a's shows rescue 0.07 to 0.12 from the move term alone.

Loadouts are planned once against a pseudoZone of species at mission level (missions.js:97-100 samples every species at mission.level; sortie.js:112 keys the cache by species count). infested-a's promoted third is fielded at level + 3 but planned against at mission level; storm-a/b and reinforcements-a patch the cache key, infested-a does not. missionProfile needs the fielded level per body or the brilliant-mind planning advantage the storm proposals claim does not exist for promoted casts.

Permadeath value. The user rates anything that prevents a death far above damage; all twelve proposals add deaths (+0.012 to +0.235 per run) and none adds a lever that prevents one. The only readable 'leave now' signals are reinforcements-a's countdown and hunted-a's HP gate. A complication whose counterplay is a death-prevention action (a window in which the retreat order is free again, a spotter kill that cancels an arrival the squad can see) would fit the stated values; none was proposed.

Register. Proposed log lines include 'The paper was wrong: <label> is here for them', 'The floor gives way', 'the pack closes in', 'come out of the dark', 'The informant left': narrative, not the mechanic and the number (ui-prose-engineer-style). Every new line should read like the existing 'Complications: Storm' and 'wave 2 of 4' lines: what spawned, where, at what distance, and which term changed.

Save compatibility of board offers. A held board offer or saved run rolled before the build carries a twist id whose row now has mods or a cast function; the pursuit lens stales such offers through MT.current, the arrivals lens does not (a saved 'reinforcements' contract pays x1.25 with no column until the board rerolls), and the terrain lens derives mods from mission.twists so old runs change behaviour mid-run on reload. One rule for 'an offer rolled under an older table' is needed across all rows.

No proposal measured on a real save with gear and potions (all say so) or with the two-twist pairs the board can roll; and no proposal gives the overseer a repeatable command in test/ that reproduces its headline numbers, which test/sortie.harness.js's OUT/diff mode already supports.

conflicts: Alternatives on one row: storm-a/storm-b, trap-a/trap-b, reinforcements-a/reinforcements-b, infested-a/infested-b, hunted-a/hunted-b each re-add the same TWISTS id with different mods keys, MOD_TEXT lines, weights and only/not lists; at most one per row can land, and the arrivals lens did not say so for its two pairs.

Three incompatible price rules. Terrain: R = p0/p1 + (d1 - d0) x PULL_COST(100) / (p1 x W0), no drops. Arrivals: m = (W0 F0 + L0 + 200 dd - L1) / (W1 F1), a death costs 200 and kill drops count. Pursuit: the measured relative rise in deaths, no formula. On the same inputs hunted-a is 1.19 (terrain rule), 1.24 (arrivals rule) or 1.4 (as proposed); turncoat-a at levels 1-4 is about 1.08 against 1.5; infested-a is 1.31 against 1.50; storm-a is 1.05 against about 1.10. u-honesty's MT.factors prints these multipliers side by side on one card, so the six rows must be priced by one rule.

Weight budget. u-honesty's draw rule is odds x min(1, poolWeight / TWIST_FULL) with TWIST_FULL = 66 and the promise that adding rows leaves the others unchanged 'until the weights sum to 66'. The original nine rows sum to 84; with the A variants the per-type pool is 75-87, with the B variants 64-96 (reinforcements-b 24, infested-b 13, turncoat-a 12), so the cap binds everywhere: my simulation (60000 rolls per level) has night 7.89% to 7.51%, dry 6.49% to 6.02%, hardcore 5.67% to 5.19% at level 10 under the A weights, and each lens computed its own frequency under a different pool (pursuit: three live rows plus its own; terrain: the same; arrivals: all nine on the current rule). One owner must set TWIST_FULL to the real total or rescale the weights.

Four cue-spawn mechanisms for one idea. reinforcements-a/b: cast groups with arrive {on, delay} and a fired flag in map.spawns, march stance, contactAt/spottedAt; hunted-a/b: TEMPORAL 'trail', cued(), counters.trailed, stance trail/pack with their own chooseGoals branches and taskGoal/rally skips; trap-a: springAmbush with ringTile and a mark; all walk a new hostile group onto the map on a cue and give it a goal rule. The axes memory asks for one mechanism with data ({on, delay, from, stance}) read by one spawner and one goal branch; the pursuit lens itself says the stance code 'should land once'.
hunted-b and reinforcements-a are the same effect (bodies arriving from the entry behind the squad) under two labels and two prices (x1.4 and x1.25); the pursuit lens says do not approve both.

Trial roads. hunted-a/b and turncoat-a/b add trial: false and a rollTwists filter; storm, trap, reinforcements and infested do not, so a one-body solo trial can roll Reinforcements, Infested or Storm. The claim that quests.js:116 passes trial: true is false today (mt.roll(type, { level, name }); roll() has no trial option), so whichever lands first must thread it.

u-retreat's contacted() is extended three ways: trap-a adds !!s.trapped, reinforcements-a mirrors it with s.contactAt set in look() and openSkirmish(), hunted pre-marks followers spotted to stay out of it; one definition of contact, in one place, before any of these.

MOD_TEXT shape. u-honesty specifies a static table keyed by mod; terrain and arrivals generate per-contract text (member lines, 'x bodies on this paper', species tags), so the honesty API must take (mods, mission) before these build; infested-b's and reinforcements-a's cards cannot be produced from the static table.

All three lenses say wave 1 is editing field.js, sortie.js, combat.js and missiontypes.js. Wave 1 is finished (.team-backup/r1w1, project files dated 01:xx-03:06); wave 2 started at 03:09 (.team-backup/r1w2) and holds u-honesty, u-retreat, u-wounds, u-ledger, u-readout and u-debrief, which touch every file these twelve cite. Every line number here moves before any of them builds, and none lists after: ['u-honesty', 'u-retreat'] in a form the scheduler reads.
missed: u-honesty is approved but not built: missiontypes.js has no modsOf, MOD_TEXT, MT.current, MT.factors or TWIST_FULL (grep across *.js is empty) and its spec moves the six rows out of TWISTS into a comment block. All twelve proposals write MODS entries against that API and re-add rows it removes; none states the dependency as a build order, and a builder landing before it would write a second, incompatible fold.

None of the three lenses used test/sortie.harness.js (u-harness, approved and present: boots game.html's script list through test/game.boot.js and plays real Sortie launch/skip/settle with combat.js, gear, potions, Condition pools and Outfit). Each wrote a private runner that re-implements resolve(), tick() regen and nameCast with gearless parties; every absolute death rate is an upper bound by the builders' own admission, and every multiplier is priced on those numbers. The field-balance-harness memory says to quote game figures from sortie.harness.js.

Storm and the window clock: escort, assassination, rescue, pursuit, sabotage and capture carry deadline: true (missiontypes.js:409, :524, :595, :618, :640, :708), exitFor (:195) gives them the window exit, and shutsAt is mission.duration (field.js:1313). Walking x0.8 shortens the usable window by 20% on six types; neither storm design scales or discloses it (only Hardcore's escalate seconds are scaled).

escalate() (field.js:1557-1560) and the window-shut branch (:1373-1376) respawn 50% / 30% of every hostile and patrol spawn group with no check for deferred, at, arrive or follows, so any twist that adds a cast group gets it cloned on escalation and on every window shut. reinforcements-a skips its groups; hunted-a and hunted-b do not.

Stale offers: boards re-roll every 6 minutes (sortie.js:97) but trial offers persist per character until the star changes (quests.js:112); any twist that changes the cast at roll time (reinforcements-a/b, infested-a/b, hunted-a/b) leaves already-rolled offers carrying the tag with no bodies behind it and the multiplier still applied. Only hunted-a proposes an MT.current cast check.

describe().hostiles (missiontypes.js:1047) sums hostile+patrol+mark counts in m.cast; the card's hostile figure includes a column or follower unless excluded. hunted-a excludes follows groups; reinforcements-a/b do not.

combat.js types a spell's main strike by strikes[0].type (:303) and its splash as 'arcane' (:308); storm-a's per-type damage multiplier misses heat splash. Riposte (:215) uses the target's damageType and DoT (:593) the condition's type, so those paths are covered.

trap-a sets s.doneAt = null at the spring; verdict() (field.js:1636) withdraws with 'this is going nowhere' when !s.withdrew && !s.doneAt && s.clock >= duration x ABANDON (2.5), so a late squad is pulled out at the moment the ambush appears.

The measured cost of hunted-a, hunted-b and part of reinforcements-a is a body on the route home (hunted-a: 49 of 52 follower-fight deaths after leaving; hunted-b: 84 of 86; reinforcements-a: 26% of firings after the walk home starts), while the tooltips describe triggers (HP under 70%, commit at 60%, contact + 45 s) that the builders' own sensitivity tables show barely move the outcome. Under the traceable-numbers rule the card has to name the thing that costs.

Positive levelOffset is new to the engine: SWARMED (field.js:84) clamps it to 0.15 and feeds makeActor hp/power (:1682-1683) and every odds() call tactics makes; infested-a includes the fix, but nothing else that reads levelOffset was audited for the sign (bestiary brief, noteSighting and castLevel add it correctly; the plain harness and tactics tests assume it is negative).

Perf was measured for one proposal only (infested-b: hostiles per run 13 to 24, 35 at level 8, Node only). turncoat-b puts an actor scan under found()/known() (10 call sites in field.js, several inside per-actor filters per step); trap-b rebuilds the map mid-run; reinforcements-b scans the whole tile grid once per call. None was timed in the browser.

Evidence slips that do not change verdicts but should be corrected in the specs: terrain's fire-word class list (classes.js has mastery 'fire' in grenadier :466, artillerist :566 and kineticist :999, not arcanist or elemental_mage; the picker line must come from Classes.lexiconOf at classes.js:1818, which the proposal does name); pursuit's 'quests.js:116 passes trial: true' (it passes level and name only); the 1950-run storm figures and all trap figures are not in any results file in the scratchpad (proto/out holds storm_random.txt at n=1500 with different death rates, storm_b_wet.txt and storm_b_cands.txt), while every pursuit log and the arrivals final-n100 files reproduce the quoted numbers.
